title: You don’t fall off the altar once.
paragraphs:
You don’t fall off the altar once.
You climb down… slowly… quietly… daily.

No one sees it.
No loud rebellion.
Just small compromises.
And that’s what makes it dangerous.

Because you can still look like a believer—
and live like you’ve taken your life back.

You posted the verse.
You sang the songs.
You lifted your hands.
There’s a part of you you won’t surrender.

That habit you keep revisiting.
That thought life you keep excusing.
That private sin you renamed “struggle” so it doesn’t sound like rebellion.
You didn’t walk away from God…
You just stopped staying on the altar.
Here’s the truth that cuts deep:
It doesn’t stay secret. It shapes you.
It hardens your heart in silence.
It numbs your conviction until wrong starts feeling normal.
Scripture doesn’t whisper about this. It confronts it.
“Offer your bodies as a living sacrifice, holy and pleasing to God—this is your true and proper worship.” — Romans 12:1
Some scholars interpret this as Paul calling believers to a continual, ongoing act of surrender—not a one-time event, but a repeated, conscious offering of every part of life to God.

Your body.
Your desires.
Your impulses.
Your hidden world.
Because God isn’t asking for a version of you.
He’s asking for all of you.
And this is where it gets uncomfortable.

It burns your pride.
It burns your excuses.
It burns your right to control your own life.
That’s why we keep climbing down.
Because surrender feels like loss… before it feels like freedom.
You are not the sacrifice that earns God’s love.
“God shows his love for us in that while we were still sinners, Christ died for us.” — Romans 5:8

Before you cleaned up.
Before you fixed your habits.
Before you got serious.
“For all have sinned and fall short of the glory of God.” — Romans 3:23
“For the wages of sin is death…” — Romans 6:23
But God didn’t leave you there.

He lived the life you couldn’t live.
He died the death you deserved.
He rose again, defeating sin and death completely.
“…but the free gift of God is eternal life in Christ Jesus our Lord.” — Romans 6:23
So when God calls you to be a living sacrifice…
He’s not trying to take life from you.
He’s trying to give you the life you’ve been resisting.
Because the version of you that clings to sin?
But the version of you surrendered to Christ?
You don’t surrender to become loved.
You surrender because you already are.
What part of your life keeps crawling off the altar?
What are you still holding back?
What have you been justifying… that God has already called you to lay down?
Because grace is not just forgiveness.
“Therefore, if anyone is in Christ, he is a new creation. The old has passed away; behold, the new has come.” — 2 Corinthians 5:17

With your pride.
With your addiction.
With your hidden battles.
With your divided heart.
Because the altar is not where God destroys you.
From hidden struggle to holy surrender—because Jesus changes everything.
